title: Native Photo CD transition boundary shows field lines
symptom: After correction of the stable interlaced Photo CD picture, horizontal field structure remains visible only in the moving transition line or transition area. The rest of the frame and the settled destination picture look correct.
expected: Determine whether the native application intentionally updates a drawmap across fields or whether E-Di publishes a partial update at the wrong field boundary. Do not deinterlace or filter the settled picture.

input_events: launch a Photo CD through its native CD-i application

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The native application may intentionally reveal an in-progress drawmap update or wipe across successive television fields. A progressive capture then exposes field structure only at the moving boundary while stable regions remain coherent.
supporting_evidence: The artifact is confined to the moving transition line or area.
The settled source and destination pictures are clean after the retained-row phase correction.
Other CD-i transitions tested by the user, including Philips FMVDemo's VMPEG path, do not show this interlacing.
CD-i applications can update display files and drawmaps incrementally while the display remains active.
contradicting_evidence: No real-hardware transition capture is currently available.
No consecutive-field provenance capture covers the transition itself.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Capture every field from immediately before the transition until it settles, including guest writes, PCL destination, decoded planes, and composed raster. If guest plane memory already contains the boundary-specific field structure before composition, the transition is authored or guest-timed.
citations: MCD212 Technical Specification section 5.2.2 and Table 5-8
Green Book UCM drawmap transfer and display operations

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: E-Di may sample or publish a guest drawmap update one field too early, exposing a narrow old/new-field mismatch only where the transition is changing.
supporting_evidence: The defect follows the changing boundary instead of remaining fixed in the picture.
The display path retains two fields, so write ownership and publication timing can affect a partial region without corrupting the settled frame.
contradicting_evidence: The corrected stable weave and its device-level phase test pass.
The absence of comparable lines in FMVDemo transitions weakens a global frontend or universal field-publication explanation, although VMPEG uses a materially different external-video path.
No diagnostic yet shows a guest write racing the rendered field.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Compare guest write timing and per-field plane hashes with the first composed field that exposes each transition row. If publication follows the programmed hardware boundary and matches guest data, emulator publication timing is not the cause.

context.scenario: Stable native Photo CD picture captured for four consecutive fields; moving wipe not yet captured

experiments.strategy: Extend the existing display diagnostic shortcut to capture a bounded 1-120 fields and summarize hashes, changed-byte bounds, and changed runs without retaining media in tracked data.
experiments.expected: A later 50/60-field capture can locate the first stage that changes at the moving wipe boundary without altering presentation behavior.
experiments.actual: The existing stable four-field capture had identical composed-raster hashes; plane A changed only 16, 32, and 33 bytes between later fields. It did not contain the moving transition and therefore neither confirms nor falsifies either incident hypothesis.
improvements: A moving transition can now be captured in one bounded request and reduced to a payload-free field summary.
experiments.evidence_quality: medium for stable-field behavior; insufficient for the reported moving boundary
experiments.confidence: high that the existing capture did not reproduce the incident

conditions: Native Photo CD base-plane output at a stable displayed picture
invalidated_by: Changes to MCD212 field retention or diagnostic plane capture
repeat_when: The shortcut can be triggered immediately before a native Photo CD moving transition

manual_verification.notes: The user confirmed the corrected stable Photo CD output looks good and clarified that remaining interlace lines are visible only in the transition line or area while it moves. Other tested CD-i transitions, including Philips FMVDemo, do not show the same effect; FMVDemo is an external VMPEG path rather than the native Photo CD base-plane path.
The user noticed no presentation difference in native Photo CD transitions. This was expected from the diagnostic-only field-capture tooling; the moving-boundary incident remains open.
